## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Migration 3 must preserve legacy email values before dropping the column. Migration 4 also needs a restore path that can reload its backup after the schema changes.

## Changes

The pull request adds migrations that drop `users.legacy_email` and `orders.coupon_code`. It snapshots `orders` before the drop and adds a test that checks both column removals and the backed-up coupon value.

## Critical

- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Back up legacy emails before dropping the column — A user added after migration 2 loses their `legacy_email` when migration 3 runs. Migration 3 drops the column without taking the snapshot described in `migrations/safety.py:3`. — Operators cannot recover that user's legacy email from the migration backups. — Fix: Call `backup_table(conn, "users", VERSION)` before the `ALTER TABLE`, following `migrations/m0002_drop_nickname.py:7`.

## Important

- migrations/m0004_drop_coupon_code.py:8 — correctness — Restore the coupon column before copying backup rows — After migration 4 runs on an order with coupon code `SPRING`, restoring the new backup fails because `migrations/safety.py:15` inserts four values per row into the three-column `orders` table. — Operators must recover the coupon manually, and a restore on an autocommit connection deletes live orders before the insert fails. — Fix: Update `migrations/safety.py:13` to restore the backed-up schema before replacing rows and perform the restore in one transaction.
